title: Principles and Algorithms for Forecasting Groups of Time Series: Locality and Globality
authors_or_org: Pablo Montero-Manso and Rob J. Hyndman
published_or_version: arXiv v3, 2021-03-26; IJF 37(4), 1632–1653, 2021; author publication page dates publication 2021-05-10
supported_claim: Sections 2–3 distinguish whole-history representational equivalence, finite-memory exceptions, and conditional generalization arguments for local/global forecasts.
limitations: Existence does not rank fitted algorithms. Panel-average bounds impose independent-series, bounded-loss and effective-sample assumptions. No enterprise AI-spend validation.
license_status: HTML explicitly identifies arXiv perpetual non-exclusive distribution license; no general code/data reuse license established.

title: Stan User’s Guide: Regression Models — Hierarchical regression
published_or_version: Version 2.40 shown on page; publication date not verified
supported_claim: Complete/no/partial pooling and multivariate hierarchical coefficient priors provide a concrete modeling vocabulary for heterogeneous groups.
limitations: Illustrative regression models are not a validated spend forecasting system; prior and likelihood sensitivity remain. A software documentation example does not establish predictive superiority.
license_status: Reuse license of this documentation page not verified; no code copied.

title: Understanding and Improving Information Transfer in Multi-Task Learning
authors_or_org: Sen Wu, Hongyang R. Zhang and Christopher Ré
supported_claim: Shared-representation multi-task learning can suffer negative transfer from task-data misalignment; conditions and experiments examine alignment and reweighting.
limitations: Theory is architecture/assumption specific; empirical tasks are NLP and images. Transfer to enterprise series is an inference, not a demonstrated result.
license_status: arXiv license link verified as perpetual non-exclusive distribution license; broader reuse and associated code license not verified.

title: Ensembles of Localised Models for Time Series Forecasting
authors_or_org: Rakshitha Godahewa, Kasun Bandara, Geoffrey I. Webb, Slawek Smyl and Christoph Bergmeir
supported_claim: Localized/clustered global ensembles and specialist approaches can improve over baseline global and univariate models; evaluation uses eight public datasets.
limitations: No demonstrated correspondence between benchmark clusters and enterprise roles/projects; clustering adds selection cost and can be unstable with short histories.
license_status: arXiv license link verified as perpetual non-exclusive distribution license; repository and dataset reuse licenses not assessed.

title: DeepAR: Probabilistic Forecasting with Autoregressive Recurrent Networks
authors_or_org: David Salinas, Valentin Flunkert and Jan Gasthaus (arXiv author listing)
supported_claim: A shared autoregressive recurrent model trained across related series is a concrete probabilistic global forecasting candidate.
limitations: Benchmark results do not imply accuracy with a few enterprise teams or zero-history users; sharing parameters is not by itself a joint dependence model across employees.
license_status: arXiv license link verified as perpetual non-exclusive distribution license; implementation and data licenses not verified.

title: Deep Factors for Forecasting
authors_or_org: Yuyang Wang, Alex Smola, Danielle Maddix, Jan Gasthaus, Dean Foster and Tim Januschowski
published_or_version: ICML 2019, PMLR 97:6607–6617; 9–15 June 2019 conference dates in proceedings metadata
supported_claim: Global latent deep structure plus local probabilistic components is a hybrid alternative; exchangeability motivates the theoretical decomposition.
limitations: Assumptions and benchmark populations need examination before use for enterprise AI spending; not evidence that a neural hybrid is required.
license_status: Page carries authors/PMLR copyright footer; exact article/code/data reuse license not verified.

title: lme4: Mixed-effects models in R
authors_or_org: Douglas Bates, Martin Maechler, Ben Bolker and Steven Walker
published_or_version: Documentation displays version 1.1-37.9000; page publication date not verified
supported_claim: Nested and crossed random effects and generalized linear mixed models are supported modeling structures, so organization levels need not be forced into a single tree.
limitations: Capability documentation, not a comparison proving that crossed effects improve this target. Sparse intersections may be unidentified.
license_status: Package page explicitly states GPL (>=2); no inference made about licenses of unrelated datasets or other implementations.

title: Optimal forecast reconciliation for hierarchical and grouped time series through trace minimization
authors_or_org: Shanika L. Wickramasuriya, George Athanasopoulos and Rob J. Hyndman
kind: Primary author publication page describing research paper
supported_claim: Reconciliation enforces aggregation coherence and uses forecast-error covariance; MinT's optimization claim is conditional on its formulation and unbiasedness assumptions.
limitations: Covariance estimation and changing aggregation structures are practical issues; coherent forecasts need not be calibrated or accurate for enterprise workloads.
license_status: Author site copyright shown; article, implementation and data reuse licenses not verified.
